newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Bejing Datang HK IPO 80 times subscribed.
newsitem.headline: Bejing Datang HK IPO 80 times subscribed.

text.p: Beijing Datang Power Generation co Ltd said on Tuesday that its initial public offer of 124.41 million H-shares in Hong Kong had been 80 times subscribed and the issue price fixed at HK$2.52 per share.

Datang Power operates coal-fired power plants which supply electricity to Beijing and other industrial cities in northern China. It said in a statement that it had received applications for 9.99 billion H-shares compared with a total 124.41 million on offer in Hong Kong.
It said an additional 157.0 million shares had been made available in the Hong Kong public offering, bringing the total flotation here to 281.41 million shares.
New World Infrastructure Ltd was allocated 492.65 million H-shares, or 9.9 percent of Datang's enlarged issued share capital, at the issue price of HK$2.52 per share.

New World Infrastructure said in a separate statement that it would obtain bank loans to finance the purchase. The bank financing would not have a material adverse effect on its cash flow and gearing, it said.
New World Infrastructure said it would hold the shares as an investment and would not dispose of them for a period of 12 months.
Dealing in Datang Power shares is expected to begin on March 21 in Hong Kong and London.
Datang Power offered a total 1.244 billion new H-shares in a global flotation at HK$2.22 to HK$2.52 per share.

Of the total, 627.01 million H-shares were initially planned to be placed with professional and institutional investors, 492.65 million to New World Infrastructure and the remaining 124.41 million shares to the public in Hong Kong.
The placing portion was reduced to 470 million H-shares from 627.01 million after the reallocation of 157 million shares to the Hong Kong public offering from the placing.
H-shares are shares of mainland Chinese companies listed in Hong Kong.
Datang Power is a subsidiary of North China Power Group Co, a state-owned enterprise controlled by the Ministry of Electric Power.
